actual_reasoning: For k>=1, the first-k-column count equals sum_i min(lambda_i,k)=n-sum_i max(lambda_i-k,0). Weak decrease makes this latter sum the maximum over row-prefix sums minus r*k, attained at the count of rows longer than k. Dominance compares every row prefix, hence these maxima, and subtraction from the same n reverses the conjugate prefix inequalities. Conjugation involution gives the reverse implication by applying the proved forward implication to mu-prime and lambda-prime. For n=0 all padded prefixes and maxima are zero and conjugation fixes the empty partition. No hypothesis or argument needs repair.
